  replaying a stateful terminal protocol, including cursor motion and destructive edits,
  against a fixed-size screen model. Resizing adds another complication: the emulator changes
  the grid dimensions and may reflow wrapped scrollback, while the PTY informs the running
  program of the new row and column count.

    1 +- ANSI escape sequences can move the cursor and erase or replace terminal content.
    2 +- Select Graphic Rendition (SGR) sequences control colors, emphasis, and other text att
       ributes.
    3 +- Escape sequences are stateful control instructions whose bytes may arrive in incomple
       te chunks.

• Created notes.md.

  - Cursor movement and content editing: These sequences let interactive programs update
    selected parts of the screen instead of printing an entirely new display for every change.
    Shell prompts, progress indicators, full-screen editors, and monitoring dashboards all
    rely on cursor positioning and erase operations. Without them, terminal output would
    behave mainly like an ever-growing paper log.

  - Select Graphic Rendition: SGR sequences attach visual meaning to text through foreground
    and background colors, bold or faint intensity, underlining, and related attributes.
    Programs use these styles to distinguish errors, warnings, commands, selections, and
    syntax. Because styles remain active until changed or reset, applications must manage them
    carefully; a missing reset can accidentally color everything printed afterward.
